analysis:
The supplied units are head-side CHANGELOG.md text, which holds prose release notes for v0.10.0 through v0.10.1 and the MLX sync. The PR hunk itself (lines 11-176 on head) is only partially visible, so the new v0.10.5 entry text, including the sandbox add-on installer notes, was not available. These units contain no executable code, so I found no concrete security regression.

Release-note statements I checked against the threat model:
- Prefix cache (T-041): complete SSD checkpoints are now stored per provider build, and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 opt-out is retained. This is consistent with the existing T-041 posture of HMAC-keyed names, a 30-minute TTL and coordinator-authored scope. The notes describe no loosening.
- Autopilot downloads (TB-011, A-018): documented as on by default for Macs with saved consent, bounded by a 50 GiB free-disk floor and optional limits, and verified downloads only. I did not verify the implementation and the notes are not evidence of a flaw.
- Desktop API, sandbox and installer (TB-013, T-061): the lines I saw describe an authenticated loopback API and a scoped desktop_account device-code purpose. The v0.10.5 sandbox installer notes are in the truncated patch region, so the TB-013 and T-061 installer-trust questions remain unverified here.
- Logprobs refusals, GLM 422 validation and the weight-hash shortcut: GLM records a verified hash in ~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json, which is owner-only, and revalidates device, inode, size, mtime and ctime. This metadata-based skip of rehashing is relevant to T-012 and T-027 (operator weight substitution) and needs code-level review if the implementing source changes appear elsewhere in the PR. A same-UID operator is already the adversary there, so this documentation alone does not show a regression.

No threat-model update is demonstrably required from these text lines. A reviewer of the code units should look at the verified-weights record, the Autopilot downloads default and the sandbox installer path.
